claims.text: Resistance of high-entropy alloys to simultaneous wear and corrosion is governed by a stable, self-healing, multicomponent oxide film.
Synergistic interactions among the alloy's diverse elements generate the protective oxide film.
The oxide film concurrently minimizes mechanical material removal and slows chemical attack.
The proposed initial alloy has a uniform multiphase microstructure and contains oxide-passivating elements such as Cr or Al.
Chemical inhibition or surface modification will disrupt oxide formation relative to natural oxide development.
The integrity and self-healing capability of the multicomponent oxide layer mediate wear-corrosion resistance.
The oxide film acts as a physical barrier against abrasive forces.
The oxide film limits ion diffusion and corrosive reactions.
After mechanical damage, the oxide film rapidly repairs itself and maintains protection under dynamic conditions.
Samples possessing a robust, self-healing oxide film will have lower combined degradation rates than samples in which oxide formation is inhibited.
Samples possessing the protective film will have lower wear-related material loss than oxide-inhibited samples.
Protective-film samples will exhibit higher electrochemical impedance and lower current density.
The protective mechanism should operate under moderate to severe conditions when the alloy chemistry permits oxide formation.
Extremely high mechanical loads can reduce or eliminate the protective effect.
Species that actively destabilize the oxide can reduce or eliminate the protective effect.
Mass-loss measurements under simultaneous wear-corrosion conditions quantify the wear component.
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and potentiodynamic polarization can assess the corrosion behavior during the comparison.
Failure of oxide-inhibited samples to show statistically higher degradation in both wear and corrosion metrics would falsify the proposed protective role.

contradictions.description: The intervention defines the natural-oxide sample as the protected comparator against an oxide-inhibited sample, and the first outcome prediction follows that comparison. The next sentence instead says the improved wear and corrosion metrics are relative to a baseline that is itself untreated and naturally oxidized, leaving no distinct protected test group and reversing or obscuring the intended comparison.
